packet.title: Kotlin core (implementation, here)
packet.summary: Adds the JVM half of the Kotlin binding in bindings/kotlin/: JNI glue whose natives each take one object, the XPath classes and their tests under ctest kotlin/jvm.

body.p: (): bindings/kotlin/ (glue, sxml_kotlin.map, the binding, 36 tests), tools/run-kotlin-tests.sh, ctest kotlin/jvm; Kotlin 2.2.20 on JDK 21, 0 leaks. The JVM half only; Android is 6.6's. After and . Owns new bindings/kotlin/: CMakeLists.txt (target sxml_kotlin, a shared library of the library, the host shim and the glue, with a version script exporting Java_* and JNI_OnLoad only), src/main/c/sxml_kotlin_jni.c, src/main/kotlin/ (Processor, Value, XPathExpression, Resolver, ResourceKind, Status, SxmlException, the internal Native object and request classes), src/test/kotlin/ (the package tests), and tools/run-kotlin-tests.sh.

item.p: JNI rules (): every native is (JNIEnv *environment, jclass owner, jobject request), three parameters, where is an internal object.
Its fields are read with field IDs that a per-processor table caches. The table lives in the processor's glue state, not in globals.
Results and failures go back into the same object: the handle, a NativeError and the side results.

The resolver bridge is a Kotlin method on the processor's internal state. It catches what the user's resolver throws, keeps it, and returns a failure. The call then rethrows it from Kotlin, so the glue never handles a pending JVM exception.
The glue follows docs/C_GUIDELINES.md (spelled-out names, no globals, no recursion). It is linted like the rest of bindings/.
ctest kotlin/jvm passes the XPath half of the parity list, the close and Cleaner tests and a two-thread test, with 0 leaks;
clang-tidy is clean on the glue.

body.p: Golden: bindings/javascript/src/index.ts for the shape and the host shim for the C.
